layout:

- The side column ends at 1250.9px, level with the bottom of the strip, also 1250.9px.
- The bar at the foot is 1198 x 76 and holds only the three numbered steps. At the left: mark 1 (24 x 24 navy circle), 8px gap, "Pick a template to start from" (331 x 52, 17.5px words, 1.5px navy border). At the right, 24px apart: mark 2 then "Send a test to me" (181 x 46), and mark 3 then the gold "Send to 167 people" (212 x 46) with its arrow (42 x 46). Spec says header "about 80px"; mine is 90px (91 with the frame's top border). The From line is 47px rather than 36px to 40px because More options must be 40px or taller with even 3px gaps above and below. The sheet gains about 20px, not the 30 or so a true 80px header would give. If K wants the letter higher still, the next cut is the Subject line at 36px.

per_file.verdict: A whole, calm layout that gives the letter the most room (684px against 630px), but it can only do that by cutting the From name short to "Louisiana Chess Ass…".
per_file.strengths: From, Subject and More options sit on one 46px row (272, 378 and 140 wide), so the letter starts a whole row higher. Subject shows in full. The toolbar has no Write it and Undo has its word back. The foot bar reads 1 Pick a template to start from, 2 Send a test to me, 3 Send to 167 people, with the three marks drawn alike and nothing wrapped or touching. The right column ends level with the strip (1250.9 and 1250.9). On the phone every control is 44px or taller and More options sits at the right of the tools row's second line.
per_file.weaknesses: The From name is cut off with an ellipsis, and the sender is the one thing a club rep most needs to check (the full name is only in the button's tooltip). The row is dense: three bordered boxes 8px apart. To fit, the phone's Add button loses its small chevron and both buttons on that line drop to 13.5px words.

per_file.verdict: The most familiar layout and the easiest to read, with full-width boxed fields and the two secondary buttons grouped at the right, but it barely adds to the letter (638px against 630px).
per_file.strengths: From and Subject are 496 x 46 each, show every word, and look like a mail program's head. More options (cream, sliders mark, chevron) and Make bigger (white, expand mark) are 200 x 46 each and stand at the right, right-aligned with the column. The strip under the letter goes back to only "Pull to make taller". The foot bar, toolbar and right column are as in A and C, and the right column ends level with the strip at 1250.9. The phone is the same as A's.
per_file.weaknesses: It gains only 8px of letter. There is 110px of empty desk between the fields and the buttons. At a glance it is the closest to the page as it is. Moving Make bigger away from the bottom of the letter undoes round 9's choice to keep the two size controls together.

per_file.verdict: The calmest of the three, and plainly different from A and B: it reads as an email being written, shows both values in full and adds 20px to the letter.
per_file.strengths: From and Subject become two slim lines (47px and 40px) inside the letter's white frame, and each press target is only as wide as its words (438 x 46 and 347 x 40). More options is a quiet 136 x 40 button at the right end of the From line, lined up with "Add a photo, event or line" below it. The full sender name is visible. The toolbar has no Write it and Undo has its word back. The foot bar is the same as in A and B, and the right column ends level with the strip. On the phone, the same header with More options at the right of the From line works: From is 215 x 56, More options 105 x 44 and Subject 328 x 44, with nothing cut off.
per_file.weaknesses: Without boxes, someone who opens the page only now and then may not see at once that From and Subject can be pressed. They have only the arrow and pencil marks, and a focus ring that a still picture cannot show. The header is 90px, not the spec's roughly 80px, so the letter gains 20px rather than about 30. On the phone the labels sit above the values, not beside them as on the computer.

changes: All three: the bar at the foot now uses the same markup and spacing everywhere. A had a 24px gap between the step 2 and step 3 groups, while B and C used Page-4's 20px, so all three now use 20px. B and C's aria labels "Start, check and send" and "Step 1, start it" are now "Pick, check and send" and "Step 1, pick a template", as in A.

All three: the heading block has the same height (155.9px). B and C's grey sentences were cut to one line: B "From and Subject stay stacked but narrower, with More options and Make bigger as two buttons at their right." and C "From and Subject become two slim lines at the top of the letter's frame, with More options at the right of the From line." B gained the "Built from / Replaces" line that A and C had. As a result, the browser frame, the bar at the foot, the caption and the phone now sit at the same height on all three boards (frame top 197.9, foot bar 1260.9, phone 1391.6).

All three: the notes box under the picture has the same style (the C layout, copied into A and B) and the same wording for items 2 and 3: "The toolbar loses “1 Write it” and its divider, and Undo has its word back." and "The mark 1 sits on Pick a template, so the bar at the foot reads 1, 2, 3." Item 1 says what each option does. Each box ends with the measured sheet height: 684px, 638px or 650px, against 630px (Page-4 measured 630.5).

B: added the three gold numbered marks in the left margin (beside the fields, the toolbar and the foot bar) to match its notes, as A and C have. Replaced B's run-on notes paragraph with the numbered list. Removed the two 'Sizes on a computer / on a phone' lists that only B had. Its phone row now uses the same 48px gap and 22px top margin as A and C.

B: More options is now drawn in Page-4's More options style (cream with the page's #c9c4b2 border, as in A and C), and Make bigger in Page-4's Make bigger style (white with the same border). Before, both had a grey-blue border and a shadow found nowhere else.

B: the phone's second tools line (Add a photo, event or line plus More options) now uses A's markup and styles, so the two options that share this phone layout draw it the same way (13.5px words, cream More options). B's phone side words were tightened to match A's.
C: the toolbar's tools are now 6px apart, as on Page-4, A and B (before, 8px moved Italic through Undo 2px to 10px right).
C: the phone's More options words went from 13px to 13.5px, the same as A and B's phone More options. It still fits beside the From value at 105 x 44.

Checked after the changes: natural heights are A 2313.7, B 2334.0 and C 2313.7, so the declared 2350 is true for all three (root and $preview). The heading, letter, right column, caption, phone letter, phone foot and tab bar text are word for word the same as Newsletter-Page-4's. Only the foot bar differs, as intended (the 1 is added and More options is gone). Each file has no animation, transition, keyframes, iframe or {{hole}}, no script other than support.js and the closing data block, no em or en dash, and no 'Start from' or USCF. Every tag is closed. Nothing is cut off or wrapped except A's From ellipsis, which is deliberate, and every computer control is 40px or taller and every phone control 44px or taller.
recommend: I recommend C, The letter's own header. People who use the page now and then see the whole sender name and subject at a glance. More options sits where K asked, in space that was going unused, and the letter gains 20px without anything feeling crowded. A gives the most letter but cuts off the From name, the thing a club rep most needs to check; B is the safest familiar layout but gains only 8px and leaves a 110px empty gap.
remaining_concerns: Each board is 2350px tall, not the spec's 1500px to 1700px estimate. A 1200 x 1140 browser frame and a 390px phone cannot sit side by side in 1440, so the phone goes underneath. That leaves about 560px of plain board background under the notes and 'On a phone' words, beside the phone. It is the same on all three boards and outside the picture of the page.
Option A cuts the From name to "Louisiana Chess Ass…". At this width it cannot fit beside a whole Subject and More options without the ellipsis.

In option C, the only signs that From and Subject can be pressed are the arrow and pencil marks; the focus ring cannot be shown in a still picture. If C is picked, the build should test whether occasional users find them, and could add a faint hover background.
Option C's header is 90px, not the spec's about 80px. A 36px Subject line would give back about 4px more if K wants the letter higher still.
Option B's 110px gap between the fields and the buttons is within the 120px limit but is the widest empty space in any of the three layouts.
On the A and B phones, "Add a photo, event or line" loses its small chevron and both buttons on that line use 13.5px words so that More options fits beside it.
The gold note marks sit outside the browser frame in the left margin. Mark 3 sits beside the foot bar's navy step 1, but the two are told apart by shape (gold square against navy circle).

I did not update the designers' sticky texts. B's report sticky said '1 Pick a template, 2 Send a test, 3 Send in the foot bar' and still holds. The sheet heights in all three reported stickies are still correct (684, 638 and 650).
